combos.t: 李东垣方。重用黄芪大补脾肺之气以资化源，“有形之血生于无形之气”，配当归养血和营。原方黄芪:当归 = 5:1（30g : 6g）。
《医学启源》方：参补气，麦冬养阴清热，五味子敛阴止汗，一补一润一敛，益气生津。用西洋参偏于清补，适合夏季气阴两伤。
《太平惠民和剂局方》补气基础方。参为君补元气，白术健脾燥湿为臣，茯苓渗湿为佐，甘草调中为使。
补血调血基础方。熟地、白芍为“血中之血药”，当归、川芎为“血中之气药”，补而不滞。
黄芪益气固表、白术健脾，是玉屏风散主体；原方另有防风以散风邪。
枸杞滋肾养肝属水，菊花清肝明目入木，取“滋水涵木”之意，即杞菊地黄丸的核心药对。
桑菊饮的主药，疏散风热、清肺明目，风热咳嗽初起常用。
清热解毒与疏风明目相合，适合风热上火、咽痛目赤。
生姜辛温走卫、大枣甘温补营，调和营卫、和胃止呕，桂枝汤等方常用。
《伤寒论》方：宣肺利咽，祛痰排脓，常用于咽痛。
《金匮要略》酸枣仁汤去知母：养血安神，清热除烦，主“虚劳虚烦不得眠”。
二陈汤缺半夏：理气燥湿化痰。
砂仁醒脾行气，可制熟地黄滋腻碍胃之弊，古有“砂仁拌熟地”之法。
陈皮理气健脾，使滋补而不壅滞。
消食化积、行气和胃，饭后积滞常用。
疏肝解郁、理气和胃，适合情志不畅兼胃胀。
清肺利咽开音，用嗓过度可短期代茶。
补益心脾、养血安神。
清肝明目，兼润肠通便。
生津通络与活血化瘀相合，现代常用于心脑血管保健思路（须遵医嘱）。
清心润肺、养肝宁神，适合虚烦失眠。
《正体类要》方：四君子汤合四物汤，气血双补。
《温病条辨》“辛凉轻剂”：疏风清热，宣肺止咳。原方用量极轻（桑叶 7.5g、菊花 3g），取“治上焦如羽，非轻不举”。
《金匮要略》方，主“妇人脏躁，喜悲伤欲哭”：养心安神，和中缓急。
由桔梗汤加玄参、麦冬而成，滋阴清热、利咽，适合阴虚咽干、用嗓过度。
闽台药膳名方：健脾祛湿、固肾止泻，性平可常服。
山楂善消肉食，麦芽善消米面，神曲善消谷积，三药合用消一切饮食积滞。
清宫御膳房方演化而来：乌梅生津敛肺，山楂消食，酸甘化阴，是消暑解渴的传统饮品。
岭南凉茶经典：清肝明目、疏风散热。
民间养血方，“以红养红”：补血养心、健脾利水。
利水渗湿、健脾，湿气重时常用；两者均偏利，津亏者不宜久服。
辛温解表、行气和胃，风寒感冒初起兼胃不适时常用。
《韩氏医通》方：黄连清心火，肉桂温肾阳、引火归元，寒热并用以交通心肾。原方黄连:肉桂约 10:1。
《伤寒论》方（原方另有鸡子黄）：黄连、黄芩清心火，阿胶、白芍滋阴血，主“心中烦，不得卧”。
《医方集解》方：女贞子冬至采、墨旱莲夏至采，故名二至。补益肝肾、滋阴止血，药性平和。
白茅根凉血利尿、芦根清热生津，二根相合清热而不伤津。
大川芎丸组成：川芎活血祛风止痛，天麻平肝息风，治头风眩晕。
理气药可制阿胶滋腻碍胃之弊。
德国家庭常备的 Fenchel-Anis-Kümmel 茶：三种伞形科种子等量，驱风消胀、解痉，成人与儿童腹胀常用。用前压碎。
德国药典“发汗茶”（Species diaphoreticae）的主体：趁热饮后保暖发汗，用于感冒初起。
英国草药传统的感冒茶，三药等量：发汗、疏风、通鼻窍。
Commission E 认可的固定组合：缬草与啤酒花协同镇静助眠，常再配香蜂草。服后勿驾驶。
欧洲最常见的健胃组合：洋甘菊解痉抗炎，薄荷驱风止呕。

formNote.zh: 所有药材均指药房或正规渠道购买的干燥饮片或茶用草药（已切制，部分经炒、炙、蒸等炮制），克数按干品计；除生姜、葱白外都不是新鲜植物。切勿自行采挖野生植物：不少有毒植物与药材外形相似，如钩吻（断肠草）与金银花、商陆与人参。
formNote.en: All herbs mean dried, cut herbs bought from a pharmacy or a reliable supplier (some stir-fried, roasted or steamed); grams are dry weight. Apart from fresh ginger and scallion, none are fresh plants. Never forage wild plants yourself: many poisonous plants look like medicinal ones, such as gelsemium and honeysuckle, or pokeweed and ginseng.

当归补血汤.t: A Li Dongyuan formula. A large dose of Huangqi strongly tonifies spleen and lung qi to support the source of blood production ("tangible blood is born from intangible qi"), paired with Danggui to nourish blood and harmonize the nutritive level. Original ratio Huangqi : Danggui = 5:1 (30g : 6g).

生脉饮.n: Generate the Pulse Drink (Sheng Mai Yin)
生脉饮.t: From Yixue Qiyuan: ginseng tonifies qi, Maidong nourishes yin and clears heat, Wuweizi preserves yin and stops sweating; one tonifies, one moistens, one astringes, together augmenting qi and generating fluids. Using American Ginseng gives a gentler, cooler tonic suited to summer damage of both qi and yin.

四君子汤.n: Four Gentlemen Decoction (Si Jun Zi Tang)
四君子汤.t: The foundational qi tonic from Taiping Huimin Hejiju Fang. Ginseng is the chief, tonifying original qi; Baizhu is the deputy, strengthening the spleen and drying dampness; Fuling is the assistant, draining dampness; Gancao is the envoy, harmonizing the middle.

四物汤.t: The foundational blood-tonifying and blood-regulating formula. Shudi and Baishao are "blood herbs within the blood"; Danggui and Chuanxiong are "qi herbs within the blood", so it tonifies without causing stagnation.

玉屏风散（缺防风）.t: Huangqi augments qi and consolidates the exterior, Baizhu strengthens the spleen; these form the core of Yu Ping Feng San. The original formula also includes Fangfeng (Saposhnikovia) to disperse wind.

桑菊药对.t: The chief herbs of Sang Ju Yin: disperse wind-heat, clear the lung and brighten the eyes; commonly used for early-stage wind-heat cough.

银菊药对.t: Combines clearing heat and resolving toxicity with dispersing wind and brightening the eyes; suited to wind-heat with internal heat, sore throat and red eyes.

姜枣药对.t: Fresh Ginger (acrid, warm) moves the defensive level; Jujube (sweet, warm) tonifies the nutritive level. Together they harmonize the nutritive and defensive qi, harmonize the stomach and stop vomiting; commonly used in Gui Zhi Tang and other formulas.

桔梗汤.t: From Shang Han Lun: diffuses the lung and soothes the throat, expels phlegm and pus; commonly used for sore throat.

酸枣仁汤意.t: Suanzaoren Tang from Jingui Yaolue without Zhimu: nourishes blood and calms the spirit, clears heat and relieves irritability; indicated for "deficiency taxation with deficiency irritability and inability to sleep".

二陈汤意.n: Two Aged Herbs Decoction (Er Chen Tang, variant)
二陈汤意.t: Er Chen Tang lacking Banxia (Pinellia): regulates qi, dries dampness and resolves phlegm.

熟地配砂仁.t: Sharen awakens the spleen and moves qi, countering the cloying, stomach-hindering nature of Shudihuang; an old method is "Shudi mixed with Sharen".

熟地配陈皮.t: Chenpi regulates qi and strengthens the spleen so that tonification does not cause congestion.

山楂配陈皮.t: Promotes digestion and dissolves accumulation, moves qi and harmonizes the stomach; commonly used for post-meal food stagnation.

玫瑰配陈皮.t: Soothes the liver and relieves constraint, regulates qi and harmonizes the stomach; suited to emotional constraint with stomach bloating.

罗汉果配胖大海.t: Clears the lung, soothes the throat and restores the voice; can be taken short-term as a tea for voice overuse.

桂圆配大枣.t: Tonifies the heart and spleen, nourishes blood and calms the spirit.

菊花配决明子.t: Clears the liver and brightens the eyes, and also moistens the intestines to unblock the bowels.

葛根配丹参.t: Combines generating fluids and unblocking the collaterals with invigorating blood and resolving stasis; commonly used in modern cardio-cerebrovascular wellness approaches (follow medical advice).

百合配酸枣仁.n: Lily Bulb with Sour Jujube Seed
百合配酸枣仁.t: Clears the heart and moistens the lung, nourishes the liver and calms the spirit; suited to deficiency irritability and insomnia.

八珍汤.t: From Zhengti Leiyao: Four Gentlemen Decoction combined with Four Substances Decoction, tonifying both qi and blood.

桑菊饮.n: Mulberry Leaf and Chrysanthemum Drink (Sang Ju Yin)
桑菊饮.t: The "light acrid-cool formula" of Wenbing Tiaobian: disperses wind and clears heat, diffuses the lung and stops cough. Original doses are very light (Sangye 7.5g, Juhua 3g), reflecting "treat the upper burner like a feather; only lightness can lift".

甘麦大枣汤.n: Licorice, Wheat and Jujube Decoction (Gan Mai Da Zao Tang)
甘麦大枣汤.t: From Jingui Yaolue, indicated for "visceral agitation in women, with a tendency to sorrow and weeping": nourishes the heart and calms the spirit, harmonizes the middle and relaxes urgency.

玄麦甘桔.t: Jiegeng Tang with Xuanshen and Maidong added: nourishes yin, clears heat and soothes the throat; suited to yin-deficient dry throat and voice overuse.

四神汤.t: A famous Fujian-Taiwan medicinal cuisine formula: strengthens the spleen and dispels dampness, consolidates the kidney and stops diarrhea; neutral in nature and suitable for regular use.

焦三仙.t: Shanzha excels at digesting meat, Maiya at flour and starches, Shenqu at grain accumulation; together they dissolve all kinds of food stagnation.

酸梅汤.t: Derived from a Qing imperial kitchen recipe: Wumei generates fluids and astringes the lung, Shanzha promotes digestion; sour and sweet combine to transform into yin. A traditional drink for relieving summer-heat and thirst.

夏桑菊.n: Prunella, Mulberry Leaf and Chrysanthemum (Xia Sang Ju)
夏桑菊.t: A classic Lingnan herbal tea: clears the liver and brightens the eyes, disperses wind and heat.

五红汤.t: A folk blood-nourishing formula, "using red to nourish red": tonifies blood and nourishes the heart, strengthens the spleen and promotes urination.

赤小豆薏米.t: Promotes urination, drains dampness and strengthens the spleen; commonly used for heavy dampness. Both are draining, so not suitable for prolonged use in those with fluid deficiency.

姜糖苏叶.t: Acrid-warm exterior release, moves qi and harmonizes the stomach; commonly used for early wind-cold common cold with stomach discomfort.

交泰丸.t: From Hanshi Yitong: Huanglian clears heart fire, Rougui warms kidney yang and guides fire back to its source; using cold and hot together to restore heart-kidney communication. Original ratio Huanglian : Rougui approx. 10:1.

黄连阿胶汤.n: Coptis and Ejiao Decoction (Huanglian Ejiao Tang)
黄连阿胶汤.t: From Shang Han Lun (the original also contains egg yolk): Huanglian and Huangqin clear heart fire, Ejiao and Baishao nourish yin and blood; indicated for "vexation in the heart with inability to lie down (sleep)".

二至丸.t: From Yifang Jijie: Nvzhenzi is harvested at the winter solstice and Mohanlian at the summer solstice, hence the name. Tonifies the liver and kidney, nourishes yin and stops bleeding; mild in nature.

茅根芦根.t: Baimaogen cools blood and promotes urination, Lugen clears heat and generates fluids; the two roots together clear heat without damaging fluids.

天麻川芎.t: The composition of Da Chuanxiong Wan: Chuanxiong invigorates blood, dispels wind and relieves pain, Tianma calms the liver and extinguishes wind; treats head-wind and dizziness.

阿胶配陈皮/砂仁.t: Qi-regulating herbs counter the cloying, stomach-hindering nature of Ejiao.

茴香三子.t: The German household Fenchel-Anis-Kümmel tea: three carrot-family seeds in equal parts, carminative and antispasmodic, used for bloating in adults and children. Crush before use.

椴花接骨木花.t: The core of the German pharmacopoeia “sweat tea” (Species diaphoreticae): drink hot, keep warm and sweat, at the onset of a cold.

蓍草接骨木花薄荷.t: The cold tea of British herbal tradition, in equal parts: promotes sweating, disperses wind and opens the nose.

缬草配啤酒花.t: A fixed combination approved by Commission E: valerian and hops act together as a sedative, often with lemon balm. Do not drive afterwards.

洋甘菊配薄荷.t: The most common European stomach pairing: chamomile relieves spasm and inflammation, peppermint is carminative and settles nausea.

玫瑰果配洛神花.t: The classic German fruit tea Hagebutte-Hibiskus: tart, thirst-quenching and deep red.

gancao|haizao.t: "Sargassum, Euphorbia, Kansui and Genkwa all oppose Licorice": Licorice is incompatible with Sargassum; using them together may increase toxicity or cause adverse reactions, and they should not be combined in a wellness formula.

dingxiang|yujin.t: "Clove must not meet Curcuma": Clove is antagonized by Curcuma Tuber; traditionally they are not used together.

renshen|laifuzi.t: Ginseng is inhibited by Radish Seed: Laifuzi directs qi downward and dissolves accumulation, weakening the qi-tonifying power of Ginseng.

xiyangshen|laifuzi.t: When ginseng-type herbs are used with Radish Seed, their qi-tonifying power is weakened by its qi-descending, digestive action.

dangshen|laifuzi.t: Dangshen tonifies and Laifuzi disperses, so the tonifying effect is reduced; may be kept if intended deliberately to "tonify without causing stagnation".
